{{nihongo|'''Keiman Shrine'''|敬満神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Tōtōmi Province]].

'''Keiman Shrine''' (Keiman Jinja<ref>[http://shizuoka-jinjacho.or.jp/shokai/jinja.php?id=4407178 Keiman Shrine] (Shizuoka Prefecture Association of Shinto Shrines).</ref> / Kyōman Jinja{{Sfn|Keiman Shrine (Heibonsha)|2000}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in Sakamoto, {{ill|Shimada, Shizuoka|ar|شيمادا (شيزوكا)|azb|شیمادا، شیزوئوکا|ce|Симада|ceb|Shimada|cs|Šimada (Šizuoka)|de|Shimada|es|Shimada|et|Shimada|fa|شیمادا، شیزوئوکا|fi|Shimada|fr|Shimada (Shizuoka)|gl|Shimada|id|Shimada, Shizuoka|it|Shimada|ja|島田市|ko|시마다시|mzn|شیمادا، شیزوئوکا|nl|Shimada|pl|Shimada|pt|Shimada|ro|Shimada|ru|Симада|simple|Shimada, Shizuoka|sv|Shimada, Shizuoka|szl|Shimada|tg|Шимада|tl|Shimada|tr|Shimada|tt|Симада|uk|Сімада (Сідзуока)|ur|شیمڈا، شیزوکا|vi|Shimada, Shizuoka|war|Shimada, Shizuoka|zh|島田市|zh_classical|島田市|zh_min_nan|Simada-chhī|zh_yue|島田|qid=Q605256}}, {{ill|Shizuoka Prefecture|Q131320|qid=Q131320}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}}), and under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=former shrine rank}} it was classified as a {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}.

=== Enshrined deities ===
The current enshrined deities are the following nine kami<ref name="Explanation board">Explanatory board within the grounds of Keiman Shrine.</ref>{{Sfn|Meiji Shrine Records|1912}}.
; Principal deity
:* '''Keiman-no-Kami''' (Kyōman-shin / Keiman-shin)
; Associated deities
:* {{ill|Sukunabikona|ca|Sukunabikona|fr|Sukunabikona|it|Sukuna-hikona|ja|スクナビコナ|ko|스쿠나비코나|mni|ꯁꯨꯀꯨꯅꯕꯤꯀꯣꯅ|pl|Sukunabikona|pt|Sukunahikona|simple|Sukunabikona|sv|Suku-Na-Bikona|zh|少彥名|qid=Q3275687|lt=Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto}}

:* {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Q272993|qid=Q272993|lt=Hayasusanoo-no-Mikoto}}
; Enshrined together

In the {{ill|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|cs|Nihon Montoku Tennó Džicuroku|de|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|es|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|ff|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|fr|Nihon Montoku tennō jitsuroku|ja|日本文徳天皇実録|ko|일본문덕천황실록|pt|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|zh|日本文德天皇實錄|qid=Q1052905}}<ref group="Original" name="Ninju 3">Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku, Ninju 3.</ref>, the deity appears as “Keiman Shinrei,” but since {{ill|Ban Nobutomo|Q4346747|qid=Q4346747}} argued in his *Banshinkō* that the deity should be identified with {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kōman Ō}}, a remote ancestor of the {{ill|Hata clan|es|Clan Hata|fa|خاندان هاتا|fr|Clan Hata|id|Klan Hata|ja|秦氏|ko|하타씨|pt|Clã Hata|zh|秦氏 (日本)|qid=Q987290}}, this theory has become known{{Sfn|History of Shimada City, Vol. 1|1978|pp=155-159}}{{Sfn|Keiman Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Keiman Shrine (Heibonsha)|2000}}. According to the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|de|Shinsen Shōjiroku|fr|Shinsen shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録|ko|신찬성씨록|ru|Синсэн сёдзироку|zh|新撰姓氏錄|qid=Q1045362}}<ref group="Original">Shinsen Shōjiroku, Left Capital, Under the Kōman Ō theory, “Keiman” is equated with “Kōman,” and based on the existence of “Hata no Kuroshige,” recorded in the {{ill|Shoku Nihon Kōki|Q1041301|qid=Q1041301}}<ref group="Original">Shoku Nihon Kōki, Jōwa 14 (847) Aug. 17.</ref> as a person of {{ill|Tōtōmi Province|Q1048864|qid=Q1048864}}{{ill|Haibara District, Shizuoka|Q1203336|qid=Q1203336|lt=Haibara District}}, it is hypothesized that the immigrant Hata clan who lived in this area enshrined their clan deity here{{Sfn|History of Shimada City, Vol. 1|1978|pp=155-159}}.

In the surrounding area to the present day, the distribution of the following three related shrines is known:
* Keiman Ōi Shrine ({{ill|Haibara District, Shizuoka|Q1203336|qid=Q1203336}}{{ill|Kawanehon|Q1204025|qid=Q1204025}} Senzu)
* Kagami-man Shrine ({{ill|Yaizu|Q696783|qid=Q696783}} Nishijima)
* Keiman Shrine (enshrined together at Hachiman Shrine in Ōhata, {{ill|Yoshida, Shizuoka|Q1202789|qid=Q1202789}}, Haibara District)
These are said to be branch shrines from Keiman Shrine (this shrine){{Sfn|History of Shimada City, Vol. 1|1978|pp=155-159}}.

=== History ===
=== Founding ===
According to shrine tradition, the founding dates to the 26th year of Emperor {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ar|الإمبراطور سوينين|arz|الامبراطور سوينين|azb|سوینین (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Suinin|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر سوینین|cs|Suinin|de|Suinin|eo|Suinin|es|Suinin Tennō|fa|امپراتور سوینین|fi|Suinin|fr|Suinin|hr|Suinin|id|Kaisar Suinin|it|Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇|ka|სუინინი|ko|스이닌 천황|lt|Imperatorius Suininas|mn|Эзэн Хаан Сүйнин|nl|Suinin|pl|Suinin|pt|Suinin|ru|Император Суйнин|sh|Car Suinin|simple|Emperor Suinin|sl|Cesar Sujnin|sr|Суинин|sv|Suinin|th|จักรพรรดิซูอินิง|tl|Emperador Suinin|tr|Suinin (imparator)|uk|Імператор Суйнін|uz|Imperator Suinin|vi|Thiên hoàng Suinin|yo|Emperor Suinin|zh|垂仁天皇|zh_min_nan|Suinin Thian-hông|zh_yue|垂仁天皇|qid=Q314850}} (the 11th emperor)<ref name="Explanation board"/>, but details are unclear. As noted above, there is a theory that it began with the enshrinement of the clan deity by the immigrant {{ill|Hata clan|es|Clan Hata|fa|خاندان هاتا|fr|Clan Hata|id|Klan Hata|ja|秦氏|ko|하타씨|pt|Clã Hata|zh|秦氏 (日本)|qid=Q987290}} who lived in the area{{Sfn|History of Shimada City, Vol. 1|1978|pp=155-159}}.

The changes in the location of enshrinement are also unclear. *Shinmyōchō Kōshō* states that it was originally near the {{ill|Ōi River|Q1044017|qid=Q1044017}} but was moved to the present location due to flooding{{Sfn|History of Shimada City, Vol. 1|1978|pp=155-159}}. Ridgepole tags indicate that it had already been enshrined at the current site by at least {{ill|Keichō|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185}} 2 ({{ill|1597|Q6790|qid=Q6790}}){{Sfn|History of Shimada City, Vol. 1|1978|pp=155-159}}. On the other hand, the discovery of a sutra mound dating to around the {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}} about 90 meters north of the precinct suggests that the ancient site of enshrinement may also have been near the present location{{Sfn|History of Shimada City, Vol. 1|1978|pp=155-159}}.

Around Keiman Shrine, the distribution of the Taniguchihara Kofun Group, including the Atagozuka Kofun (a designated historic site of Shimada City), is known{{Sfn|Taniguchi Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2000}}. This kofun group is a late {{ill|Kofun period|Q459939|qid=Q459939}} group said to have once consisted of more than 100 mounds, but the area, and even the {{ill|Makinohara Plateau|Q11570346|qid=Q11570346}}, is a region where few sites or kofun from the Yayoi period to the early Kofun period are known{{Sfn|Taniguchi Kofun Group (Heibonsha)|2000}}. Although the location of the district office of Haibara District in {{ill|Tōtōmi Province|Q1048864|qid=Q1048864}} is unknown, there is a theory that it was near Keiman Shrine{{Sfn|Haibara District (Heibonsha)|2000}}.

=== Overview ===
In the {{ill|National Histories|Q11420601|qid=Q11420601|lt=Six National Histories}}, there is an entry stating that in {{ill|Ninju|de|Ninju|es|Ninju|fa|نینجو|fr|Ère Ninju|ia|Ninju|id|Ninju|ja|仁寿|ko|닌주|ru|Ниндзю|simple|Ninju|sr|Нинџу|tr|Ninju|uk|Ніндзю|zh|仁壽 (日本)|zh_yue|仁壽 (日本)|qid=Q1373077}} 3 ({{ill|853|Q30367|qid=Q30367}})<ref group="Original" name="Ninju 3"/> “Keiman Shinrei” was granted the status of a Myōjin, and another entry stating that in {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} 2 ({{ill|860|ab|860|af|860|am|860 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|860|ar|860|ary|860|ast|860|avk|860|az|860|azb|۸۶۰ (میلادی)|ban|860|bar|860|bcl|860|be|860|be_x_old|860|bg|860|bn|৮৬০|bpy|মারি ৮৬০|br|860|bs|860.|ca|860|cdo|860 nièng|ceb|860|ckb|٨٦٠|crh|860|cs|860|csb|860|cv|860|cy|860|da|860|de|860|el|860|eml|860|eo|860|es|860|et|860|eu|860|fa|۸۶۰ (میلادی)|fi|860|fo|860|fr|860|fy|860|ga|860|gan|860年|gd|860|gl|860|he|860|hi|860|hr|860.|ht|860 (almanak jilyen)|hu|860|hy|860|id|860|ilo|860|io|860|is|860|it|860|ja|860年|jv|860|ka|860|kaa|860|kk|860 жыл|ko|860년|la|860|lb|860|lij|860|lmo|860|lt|860 m.|lv|860. gads|map_bms|860|mdf|860|mg|860|mhr|860|mk|860|mr|इ.स. ८६०|mrj|860 и|ms|860|mzn|۸۶۰|nah|860|nap|860|nds|860|new|सन् ८६०|nl|860|nn|860|no|860|nrm|860|nso|860|oc|860|or|୮୬୦|os|860-æм аз|pl|860|pnb|860|pt|860|qu|860|ro|860|ru|860 год|rue|860|sa|८६०|scn|860|sd|860ع|se|860|sh|860.|shn|860|si|860|simple|860|sk|860|sl|860|smn|860|sq|860|sr|860|su|860|sv|860|sw|860|tg|Соли 860|th|พ.ศ. 1403|tk|860|tl|860|tly|860|tr|860|tt|860 ел|uk|860|ur|860ء|uz|860|vec|860|vi|860|war|860|wuu|860年|xmf|860|zh|860年|zh_min_nan|860 nî|zh_yue|860年|qid=Q24714}})<ref group="Original" name="Jōgan 2"/> the {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|fa|شینکای (رتبه الهی)|ja|神階|qid=Q11591025}} of “Keiman-no-Kami” was promoted from Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade to Senior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade{{Sfn|Keiman Shrine (Heibonsha)|2000}}. Within {{ill|Tōtōmi Province|Q1048864|qid=Q1048864}}, this rank surpasses even that of {{ill|Okuni Shrine|Q421597|qid=Q421597}} ({{ill|Shūchi District, Shizuoka|Q1205501|qid=Q1205501}}{{ill|Mori, Shizuoka|Q1345571|qid=Q1345571|lt=Mori Town}}, the province’s Ichinomiya) and Meharakawachi Shrine (two shrines proposed by identification theory), making it the highest rank.

In the *{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}* {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Register of Deities}}, compiled in {{ill|Enchō|de|Enchō|fa|انچو|fr|Ère Enchō|ia|Encho|id|Enchō|ja|延長 (元号)|ko|엔초|ru|Энтё|simple|Enchō|sr|Енчо|tr|Enchō|uk|Ентьо|zh|延長 (日本)|zh_yue|延長 (年號)|qid=Q1327274|lt=Enchō}} 5 ({{ill|927|ab|927|af|927|am|927 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|927|ar|927|ary|927|ast|927|avk|927|az|927|azb|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|bar|927|bcl|927|be|927|be_x_old|927|bg|927|bn|৯২৭|bpy|মারি ৯২৭|br|927|bs|927.|ca|927|cdo|927 nièng|ceb|927|ckb|٩٢٧|crh|927|cs|927|csb|927|cv|927|cy|927|da|927|de|927|el|927|eml|927|eo|927|es|927|et|927|eu|927|fa|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|fi|927|fo|927|fr|927|fy|927|ga|927|gan|927年|gd|927|gl|927|he|927|hi|927|hr|927.|ht|927 (almanak jilyen)|hu|927|hy|927|id|927|ilo|927|io|927|is|927|it|927|ja|927年|jv|927|ka|927|kaa|927|kk|927 жыл|ko|927년|la|927|lb|927|lij|927|lmo|927|lt|927 m.|lv|927. gads|map_bms|927|mdf|927|mg|927|mhr|927|mi|927|mk|927|mr|इ.स. ९२७|mrj|927 и|ms|927|mzn|۹۲۷|nah|927|nap|927|nds|927|new|सन् ९२७|nl|927|nn|927|no|927|nrm|927|nso|927|oc|927|or|୯୨୭|os|927-æм аз|pl|927|pnb|927|pt|927|qu|927|ro|927|ru|927 год|rue|927|sa|९२७|scn|927|sd|927ع|se|927|sh|927.|shn|927|si|927|sk|927|smn|927|sq|927|sr|927|su|927|sv|927|sw|927|tg|Соли 927|th|พ.ศ. 1470|tk|927|tl|927|tly|927|tr|927|tt|927 ел|uk|927|ur|927ء|uz|927|vec|927|vi|927|war|927|wuu|927年|xmf|927|zh|927年|zh_min_nan|927 nî|zh_yue|927年|qid=Q30470}}), it is listed as “Keiman Shrine, Myōjin Taisha” in Haibara District of Tōtōmi Province, placing it among the {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}}{{Sfn|Keiman Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1988}}. In the same register, the reading of “Keiman” is given as “Kyōmano” or “Kyōman”{{Sfn|Keiman Shrine (Heibonsha)|2000}}. Subsequent developments during the {{ill|Middle Ages|Q12554|qid=Q12554}} are unclear{{Sfn|History of Shimada City, Vol. 1|1978|pp=155-159}}.

During the {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} era ({{ill|1573|Q6678|qid=Q6678}}–{{ill|1593|Q6772|qid=Q6772}}), the lord of {{ill|Kakegawa Domain|Q3034456|qid=Q3034456|lt=Kakegawa Domain}}, {{ill|Yamauchi Kazutoyo|Q1315878|qid=Q1315878}}, is said to have donated shrine lands{{Sfn|Keiman Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1988}}. In the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, by order of the shogunate, {{ill|Ina Tadatsugu|Q3387913|qid=Q3387913}} also donated shrine lands, and during the {{ill|Genroku|Q1325001|qid=Q1325001}} era ({{ill|1688|ab|1688|af|1688|als|1688|am|1688 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1688|ar|1688|ary|1688|arz|1688|ast|1688|avk|1688|az|1688|azb|۱۶۸۸ (میلادی)|ban|1688|bar|1688|bcl|1688|be|1688|be_x_old|1688|bg|1688|bn|১৬৮৮|bpy|মারি ১৬৮৮|br|1688|bs|1688.|ca|1688|cdo|1688 nièng|ceb|1688|ckb|١٦٨٨|crh|1688|cs|1688|cv|1688|cy|1688|da|1688|de|1688|diq|1688|el|1688|eml|1688|eo|1688|es|1688|et|1688|eu|1688|fa|۱۶۸۸ (میلادی)|fi|1688|fo|1688|fr|1688|frp|1688|frr|1688|fur|1688|fy|1688|ga|1688|gan|1688年|gcr|1688|gd|1688|gl|1688|gv|1688|he|1688|hi|१६८८|hr|1688.|hsb|1688|ht|1688 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1688|hy|1688|hyw|1688 թուական|ia|1688|id|1688|ilo|1688|io|1688|is|1688|it|1688|ja|1688年|jv|1688|ka|1688|kaa|1688|kk|1688 жыл|ko|1688년|krc|1688 джыл|ksh|Joohr 1688|la|1688|lb|1688|lij|1688|lmo|1688|lt|1688 m.|lv|1688. gads|mai|१६८८|map_bms|1688|mdf|1688|mg|1688|mhr|1688|mi|1688|mk|1688|mr|इ.स. १६८८|mrj|1688 и|ms|1688|my|၁၆၈၈|mzn|۱۶۸۸|nah|1688|nap|1688|nds|1688|new|सन् १६८८|nl|1688|nn|1688|no|1688|nrm|1688|nso|1688|oc|1688|olo|1688|or|୧୬୮୮|os|1688-æм аз|pa|1688|pl|1688|pnb|1688|pt|1688|qu|1688|ro|1688|ru|1688 год|rue|1688|sa|१६८८|sah|1688|scn|1688|sd|1688ع|se|1688|sh|1688.|shn|1688|simple|1688|sk|1688|sl|1688|smn|1688|sq|1688|sr|1688|su|1688|sv|1688|sw|1688|szl|1688|ta|1688|te|1688|tg|Соли 1688|th|พ.ศ. 2231|tk|1688|tl|1688|tly|1688|tr|1688|tt|1688 ел|uk|1688|ur|1688ء|uz|1688|vec|1688|vi|1688|vls|1688|wa|1688|war|1688|wuu|1688年|xmf|1688|yi|1688|zea|1688|zh|1688年|zh_min_nan|1688 nî|zh_yue|1688年|qid=Q7671}}–{{ill|1704|Q6824|qid=Q6824}}) 6 koku and 3 to were donated as exempt land{{Sfn|Keiman Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1988}}. Around this time, it was also called “Keiman Daibosatsu (Kagami-man Daibosatsu)”{{Sfn|Keiman Shrine (Heibonsha)|2000}}.

After the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|Q8707|qid=Q8707}}, in {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 6 ({{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}}) it was ranked as a {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}} under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=Modern system of shrine ranks}}{{Sfn|Keiman Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1988}}. In Meiji 7 ({{ill|1874|ab|1874|af|1874|als|1874|am|1874 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1874|ar|1874|ary|1874|arz|1874|ast|1874|avk|1874|az|1874|azb|۱۸۷۴ (میلادی)|ba|1874 йыл|ban|1874|bar|1874|bat_smg|1874|bcl|1874|be|1874|be_x_old|1874|bg|1874|bn|১৮৭৪|bpy|মারি ১৮৭৪|br|1874|bs|1874.|ca|1874|cdo|1874 nièng|ce|1874 шо|ceb|1874|ckb|١٨٧٤|crh|1874|cs|1874|csb|1874|cv|1874|cy|1874|da|1874|de|1874|diq|1874|el|1874|eml|1874|eo|1874|es|1874|et|1874|eu|1874|fa|۱۸۷۴|fi|1874|fiu_vro|1874|fo|1874|fr|1874|frp|1874|frr|1874|fur|1874|fy|1874|ga|1874|gan|1874年|gcr|1874|gd|1874|gl|1874|gn|1874|gv|1874|hak|1874-ngièn|he|1874|hi|१८७४|hif|1874|hr|1874.|hsb|1874|ht|1874 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1874|hy|1874|hyw|1874 թուական|ia|1874|id|1874|ilo|1874|io|1874|is|1874|it|1874|ja|1874年|jv|1874|ka|1874|kaa|1874|kk|1874 жыл|kn|೧೮೭೪|ko|1874년|krc|1874 джыл|ksh|Joohr 1874|ku|1874|kv|1874-ӧд во|la|1874|lb|1874|lez|1874 йис|li|1874|lij|1874|lmo|1874|lt|1874 m.|lv|1874. gads|mai|१८७४|map_bms|1874|mdf|1874|mg|1874|mhr|1874|mi|1874|min|1874|mk|1874|mr|इ.स. १८७४|mrj|1874 и|ms|1874|my|၁၈၇၄|myv|1874 ие|mzn|۱۸۷۴|nah|1874|nap|1874|nds|1874|nds_nl|1874|new|ई सं १८७४|nl|1874|nn|1874|no|1874|nrm|1874|nso|1874|oc|1874|olo|1874|or|୧୮୭୪|os|1874-æм аз|pa|1874|pl|1874|pms|1874|pnb|1874|pt|1874|qu|1874|ro|1874|ru|1874 год|rue|1874|sa|१८७४|sah|1874|scn|1874|sd|1874ع|se|1874|sh|1874.|shn|1874|simple|1874|sk|1874|sl|1874|smn|1874|sq|1874|sr|1874|stq|1874|su|1874|sv|1874|sw|1874|szl|1874|ta|1874|tay|kawas na 1874|te|1874|tet|1874|tg|Соли 1874|th|พ.ศ. 2417|tk|1874|tl|1874|tly|1874|tr|1874|tt|1874 ел|udm|1874 ар|uk|1874|ur|1874ء|uz|1874|vec|1874|vi|1874|vls|1874|vo|1874|wa|1874|war|1874|wuu|1874年|xmf|1874|yi|1874|za|1874 nienz|zea|1874|zh|1874年|zh_classical|一八七四年|zh_min_nan|1874 nî|zh_yue|1874年|qid=Q7761}}), nearby Suwa Shrine, Atago Shrine, Sankō Shrine, and Tenjin Shrine were enshrined together{{Sfn|Keiman Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1988}}. In Meiji 44 ({{ill|1911|Q2076|qid=Q2076}}), it was designated as a shrine receiving offerings of sacred food and ritual implements{{Sfn|Keiman Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1988}}. In {{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 21 ({{ill|1946|ab|1946|ace|1946|af|1946|als|1946|am|1946 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1946|ar|1946|ary|1946|arz|1946|ast|1946|av|1946 сон|avk|1946|az|1946|azb|۱۹۴۶ (میلادی)|ba|1946 йыл|ban|1946|bar|1946|bat_smg|1946|bcl|1946|be|1946|be_x_old|1946|bg|1946|bh|1946|bjn|1946|bn|১৯৪৬|bpy|মারি ১৯৪৬|br|1946|bs|1946.|ca|1946|cdo|1946 nièng|ce|1946 шо|ceb|1946|ckb|١٩٤٦|co|1946|crh|1946|cs|1946|csb|1946|cv|1946|cy|1946|da|1946|de|1946|diq|1946|dsb|1946|el|1946|eml|1946|eo|1946|es|1946|et|1946|eu|1946|ext|1946|fa|۱۹۴۶|fi|1946|fiu_vro|1946|fo|1946|fr|1946|frp|1946|frr|1946|fur|1946|fy|1946|ga|1946|gag|1946|gan|1946年|gcr|1946|gd|1946|gl|1946|gn|1946|gv|1946|hak|1946-ngièn|he|1946|hi|१९४६|hif|1946|hr|1946.|hsb|1946|ht|1946 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1946|hy|1946|hyw|1946 թուական|ia|1946|id|1946|ilo|1946|io|1946|is|1946|it|1946|ja|1946年|jbo|1946moi|jv|1946|ka|1946|kaa|1946|kbp|1946|kk|1946 жыл|kn|೧೯೪೬|ko|1946년|krc|1946 джыл|ksh|Joohr 1946|ku|1946|kv|1946-ӧд во|kw|1946|la|1946|lb|1946|lez|1946 йис|li|1946|lij|1946|lld|1946|lmo|1946|ln|1946|lt|1946 m.|lv|1946. gads|mai|१९४६|map_bms|1946|mdf|1946|mg|1946|mhr|1946|mi|1946|min|1946|mk|1946|ml|1946|mn|1946 он|mr|इ.स. १९४६|mrj|1946 и|ms|1946|my|၁၉၄၆|myv|1946 ие|mzn|۱۹۴۶|nah|1946|nap|1946|nds|1946|nds_nl|1946|new|ई सं १९४६|nl|1946|nn|1946|no|1946|nrm|1946|nso|1946|oc|1946|olo|1946|or|୧୯୪୬|os|1946-æм аз|pa|1946|pam|1946|pap|1946|pl|1946|pnb|1946|pt|1946|qu|1946|ro|1946|roa_tara|1946|ru|1946 год|rue|1946|sah|1946 сыл|sc|1946|scn|1946|sco|1946|sd|1946ع|se|1946|sh|1946.|shn|1946|si|1946|simple|1946|sk|1946|sl|1946|smn|1946|sq|1946|sr|1946|stq|1946|su|1946|sv|1946|sw|1946|szl|1946|ta|1946|te|1946|tet|1946|tg|Соли 1946|th|พ.ศ. 2489|tk|1946|tl|1946|tly|1946|tpi|1946|tr|1946|tt|1946 ел|ty|1946|udm|1946 ар|ug|1946 - يىلى|uk|1946|ur|1946ء|uz|1946|vec|1946|vep|1946|vi|1946|vls|1946|vo|1946|wa|1946|war|1946|xmf|1946|yi|1946|za|1946 nienz|zea|1946|zh|1946年|zh_classical|一九四六年|zh_min_nan|1946 nî|zh_yue|1946年|qid=Q18610}}) January, it was recognized as qualifying for prefectural shrine status{{Sfn|Keiman Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1988}}, but the shrine rank system was abolished in February of that year.

* {{ill|Ninju|de|Ninju|es|Ninju|fa|نینجو|fr|Ère Ninju|ia|Ninju|id|Ninju|ja|仁寿|ko|닌주|ru|Ниндзю|simple|Ninju|sr|Нинџу|tr|Ninju|uk|Ніндзю|zh|仁壽 (日本)|zh_yue|仁壽 (日本)|qid=Q1373077}} 3 ({{ill|853|Q30367|qid=Q30367}}) November 27: Granted Myōjin status (*{{ill|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|cs|Nihon Montoku Tennó Džicuroku|de|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|es|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|ff|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|fr|Nihon Montoku tennō jitsuroku|ja|日本文徳天皇実録|ko|일본문덕천황실록|pt|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|zh|日本文德天皇實錄|qid=Q1052905}}*)<ref group="Original" name="Ninju 3">Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku, Ninju 3 (853) November 27 (see {{Harvnb|Shinto and Shrine Historical Sources Collection}}).</ref> – Recorded as “Keiman Shinrei.”

The worship hall is in the {{ill|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|Q855025|qid=Q855025}} style, also with a copper-sheeted roof{{Sfn|Keiman Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1988}}.

* Ōkusu Shrine (Ōkusu Jinja)
** Location: Sakamoto, Shimada City ({{Coord|34|49|3.57|N|138|12|27.29|E|region:JP-22_type:landmark|name=Outside shrine: Ōkusu Shrine}})

** Shrine rank: Shikinaisha “Ōkusu Shrine,” former {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}
*: It is enshrined about 350 meters east of Keiman Shrine. Regarding the enshrined deities, *Tōtōmi Province Fudoki-den* compares Ōkusu Shrine and Keiman Shrine to {{ill|Oarai Isosaki Shrine|es|Santuario Ōarai Isosaki|ja|大洗磯前神社|simple|Ōarai Isosaki the latter’s to Sukunahikona-no-Kami{{Sfn|Ōkusu Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1988}}.
*: For Ōkusu Shrine, a connection has been suggested with the entry for the 62nd year of Emperor {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|Q313119|qid=Q313119}} in the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|Q813935|qid=Q813935}}<ref group="Original">Nihon Shoki, Emperor Nintoku, year 62, May.</ref>. In that entry, during a report by the governor of Tōtōmi Province, it is said that a great tree flowed down the Ōi River and stopped at a bend in the river, so {{ill|Yamato no Agoko|fr|Yamato no Agoko|ja|倭吾子籠|qid=Q55406552|lt=Yamato no Agoko}} was dispatched to build a boat and transport it to Naniwa Harbor. The “great tree” mentioned is thought to be a {{ill|Camphora officinarum|Q158722|qid=Q158722}}, and it is conjectured that Ōkusu Shrine enshrines its divine spirit<ref name="Ōkusu Shrine explanation board">Explanatory board within the grounds of Ōkusu Shrine.</ref>{{Sfn|History of Shimada City, Vol. 1|1978|pp=153-155}}{{Sfn|Ōkusu Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1988}}. According to the *Wamyōshō*, the existence of “Funaki-gō” in Haibara District of Suruga Province suggests the possibility that the area was an ancient shipbuilding site{{Sfn|History of Shimada City, Vol. 1|1978|pp=153-155}}.
*: According to the shrine tradition of Ōkusu Shrine, it was founded in the 3rd year of Emperor {{ill|Emperor Kinmei|ar|الإمبراطور كيمي|arz|الامبراطور كيمى|azb|کیم‌می (ایمپیراتور)|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر کینمێی|cs|Kinmei|de|Kimmei|es|Kinmei Tennō|fa|امپراتور کینمی|fi|Kinmei|fr|Kinmei|hr|Kinmei|id|Kaisar Kimmei|it|Kinmei|ja|欽明天皇|ka|კიმეი|ko|긴메이 천황|nl|Kimmei|pl|Kinmei|pt|Kimmei|ru|Император Киммэй|sh|Car Kimmei|simple|Emperor Kinmei|sl|Cesar Kinmei|sv|Kimmei|th|จักรพรรดิคิมเม|tl|Emperador Kimmei|tr|Kimmei (imparator)|uk|Імператор Кіммей|uz|Imperator Kinmei|vi|Thiên hoàng Kimmei|yo|Emperor Kimmei|zh|钦明天皇|zh_min_nan|Kinmei Thian-hông|zh_yue|欽明天皇|qid=Q329792}} ({{ill|542|ab|542|af|542|am|542 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|542|ar|542|ary|542|ast|542|avk|542|az|542|azb|۵۴۲ (میلادی)|bar|542|be|542|be_x_old|542|bg|542|bn|৫৪২|bpy|মারি ৫৪২|br|542|bs|542.|ca|542|cdo|542 nièng|ceb|542|ckb|٥٤٢|crh|542|cs|542|cv|542|cy|542|da|542|de|542|el|542|eml|542|eo|542|es|542|et|542|eu|542|fa|۵۴۲ (میلادی)|fi|542|fo|542|fr|542|fy|542|ga|542|gan|542年|gd|542|gl|542|he|542|hi|542|ht|542 (almanak jilyen)|hu|542|hy|542|id|542|io|542|it|542|ja|542年|jv|542|ka|542|kk|542 жыл|ko|542년|la|542|lb|542|lij|542|lmo|542|lt|542 m.|map_bms|542|mdf|542|mg|542|mhr|542|mk|542|mr|इ.स. ५४२|mrj|542 и|ms|542|mzn|۵۴۲|nah|542|nap|542|nds|542|nds_nl|542|new|सन् ५४२|nl|542|nn|542|no|542|nso|542|oc|542|or|୫୪୨|os|542-æм аз|pl|542|pnb|542|pt|542|qu|542|ro|542|ru|542 год|rue|542|sa|५४२|scn|542|sd|542ع|sh|542.|shn|542|sk|542|sl|542|sq|542|sr|542|su|542|sv|542|sw|542|tg|Соли 542|th|พ.ศ. 1085|tk|542|tl|542|tly|542|tr|542|tt|542 ел|uk|542|ur|542ء|uz|542|vec|542|vi|542|war|542|wuu|542年|xmf|542|zh|542年|zh_min_nan|542 nî|zh_yue|542年|qid=Q33631}}?)<ref name="Ōkusu Shrine explanation board"/>{{Sfn|Ōkusu Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1988}}. In the *Engishiki* Register of Deities, it is listed as a Shikinaisha small shrine in the same Haibara District as Keiman Shrine{{Sfn|Ōkusu Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1988}}. In Meiji 6 (1873) it was ranked as a village shrine, and in Meiji 44 (1911) it was merged with Keiman Shrine and became an outside shrine of Keiman Shrine{{Sfn|Ōkusu Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1988}}. Today, only a small sanctuary remains.
